chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Abu Sa'id al-Khorasani who said:

Two men entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) in Khorasan and asked him about shortening the prayer. He said to one of them, 'Shortening is obligatory upon you because you intended me,' and he said to the other, 'Completing is obligatory upon you because you intended the Sultan.'

The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And whoever completes [the prayer] while traveling is like one who shortens while resident, and it is obligatory upon him to repeat [the prayer], unless he does so out of ignorance.
To indicate this is what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated - from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man fasted while traveling.' He said, 'If it reached him that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that, then he must make up for it; and if it did not reach him, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening the prayer (performing 2 rak'ahs instead of 4)
key_terms.الْقَضَاء: Making up for missed prayers or acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What determines whether a traveler must shorten or complete their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* highlights the Shia juristic principle that the status of a traveler (musafir) is determined by the purpose of the journey, specifically distinguishing between visiting a religious authority (Imam) and a political ruler (Sultan). It establishes that completing prayers while traveling is equivalent to shortening them while resident, thereby requiring repetition (i'dad) if done without valid excuse or ignorance. The accompanying narration further clarifies the ruling for fasting while traveling, emphasizing that liability for making up the fast (qada) depends on whether the traveler was aware of the Prophet's prohibition against fasting during travel.
